lua.debug.launch.console.description: The specified console to launch the program.
lua.debug.launch.console.internalConsole: VS Code debug console (input stream not supported).
lua.debug.launch.console.externalTermina: External terminal that can be configured in user settings.
lua.debug.launch.luaVersion.description: Lua ABI of the debuggee. `auto` (the default) lets the debugger detect it in the target; any other value is a constraint the detected ABI must satisfy, and a conflict is refused. Detection needs evidence: a symbol table that only names APIs shared by Lua 5.4 and 5.5 cannot pick between them, so an explicit version is then required. It only selects the bundled `runtime/<platform>/<version>/lua` when the adapter starts one; it says nothing about an externally supplied VM.
lua.debug.launch.luaVersion.auto.descrip: Detect the ABI from the running VM. A binary that exports nothing needs a symbol table or an explicit version.
lua.debug.launch.vmSource.description: Optional description of the debuggee's Lua implementation for binaries that export nothing (statically linked, stripped, or hidden symbols).
lua.debug.launch.luaBinary.description: Path or file name of the *already loaded* Lua image to debug. Only selects among mapped modules: the full path or the file name must match exactly, nothing is loaded to satisfy it, and a file name that matches two modules is an error. Leave it unset to keep automatic discovery.
lua.debug.launch.luaSymbols.description: Optional description of the debuggee's Lua implementation for binaries that export nothing (statically linked, stripped, or hidden symbols). Each entry takes exactly one of `address` (absolute hexadecimal address in the current process; re-derive it after every restart), `offset` (non-negative hexadecimal RVA from the loaded `luaBinary` base, not a file offset; requires `luaBinary`) or `pattern` (Gum pattern such as `FD 7B ?? A9`, which must match exactly once). Only known symbol names are accepted, so a typo is rejected instead of ignored. Mutually exclusive with `luaSymbolsFile`; a large table is written to a temporary file by the adapter. For an image that exports no symbol at all, the launcher's two discovery points (requires `luaBinary`) are named by the pseudo-symbols `lua_debug_server_newstate` (a creation entry whose return value is the new `lua_State*`; kept armed) and `lua_debug_server_call` (a per-call entry whose first argument is a `lua_State*`; released when the one-minute discovery window closes). Give each one rule; with them present the launcher hooks exactly those two points.
lua.debug.launch.luaSymbolsFile.descript: UTF-8 JSON file holding the same object as `luaSymbols`, read by the target process. Mutually exclusive with `luaSymbols`. Use it for tables too large to inline.
